title: Gold leaf is cheap. Space is not.
subtitle: The most expensive thing on a good ship is the part of it nobody is standing in.

text: Decoration is a one-off cost. Space is a cost every sailing.
sub: A marble atrium is paid for once, at the shipyard. Selling four hundred berths where you could have sold nine hundred is paid for on every voyage the ship ever makes.

items.head: Guests against tonnage
items.body: The space ratio. It tells you whether the public rooms are generous or only photographed from a flattering corner.

items.head: Guests against crew
items.body: Close to one to one and service can anticipate. Stretch it and service becomes queueing, however warm the crew are.

items.head: Dining seats against beds
items.body: If the room cannot seat the ship, the reservation system is doing the rationing — and you will feel it by Wednesday.

quote: You do not notice space. You notice its absence — and then you spend the week noticing nothing else.

text: Buy the emptier ship, not the shinier one.
sub: The Cyclades in October is the same sea from either deck. The difference is whether the deck has forty people on it or four hundred, and that difference is the entire holiday.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with
body: If you send me two sailings you're weighing, I'll send back a two-line verdict on which one actually has room in it.
